curriculum_status: Unverified: no authoritative curriculum specification is bundled. Syllabus codes are version metadata only.

entries.title: Newton's laws
entries.explanation: An object maintains its velocity when the resultant external force is zero. A net force changes momentum; for constant mass, ΣF = ma. Interaction forces act on different bodies.
entries.equations: ΣF = ma; F(A on B) = −F(B on A)
entries.symbols: F: force (N); m: mass (kg); a: acceleration (m s⁻²). 1 N = 1 kg m s⁻².
entries.assumptions: Inertial frame, constant mass, speeds small compared with light. A balanced force does not require zero velocity.
entries.example: Cargo: m = 10 kg and downhill ΣF = 32.0586 N. a = 32.0586 / 10 = 3.20586 m s⁻².
entries.discovery: Mira's diagnostic pedestal and the cargo guide.

entries.title: Weight and normal reaction
entries.explanation: Weight acts toward the ground. The normal reaction is perpendicular to the contact surface. It balances the perpendicular component of weight on a straight fixed guide with no other perpendicular forces.
entries.equations: W = mg; N = mg cos θ; W∥ = mg sin θ
entries.symbols: W, N: forces (N); g: gravitational acceleration (m s⁻²); θ: ramp angle (degrees in controls).
entries.assumptions: Uniform g, fixed straight incline, maintained contact, no additional perpendicular applied force. Normal reaction is not always equal to weight.
entries.discovery: Vector Sight on the inclined cargo rail.

entries.title: Static and kinetic friction
entries.explanation: Static friction adjusts to prevent slipping until its limiting magnitude is exceeded. Kinetic friction opposes the actual motion; it changes sign for uphill motion.
entries.equations: |fₛ| ≤ μₛN; |fₖ| = μₖN; a↓ = g(sin θ − μₖ cos θ)
entries.symbols: f: friction (N); μₛ, μₖ: dimensionless coefficients; N: normal reaction (N).
entries.assumptions: Dry Coulomb friction on a fixed guide. The final acceleration formula applies to cargo already moving downhill. At rest, test mg sin θ > μₛN first.
entries.example: 10 kg, 30°, μₛ = 0.40, μₖ = 0.20: 49.05 N > 33.9828 N, so release slides; fₖ = 16.9914 N and a = 3.20586 m s⁻². At 15°, static friction is only 25.3901 N, below its limit.
entries.discovery: The Cargo Mechanism: angle changes release the crate.

entries.title: Projectile motion
entries.explanation: Horizontal velocity stays constant while gravity changes vertical velocity. The launcher and its dotted prediction use the same analytic clock and swept collision body.
entries.equations:
vₓ = u cos θ; vᵧ = u sin θ − gt
x = x₀ + u cos θ t; y = y₀ + u sin θ t − ½gt²
H = u² sin²θ / (2g); R = u² sin(2θ) / g (equal heights only)
entries.symbols: x, y, H, R: lengths (m); u, v: speeds (m s⁻¹); t: time (s); positive y is upward.
entries.assumptions: Uniform gravity, negligible drag, point trajectory with a 4 px projectile collision radius. Unequal elevations use t = [u sin θ ± √(u² sin²θ − 2gΔy)] / g; retain positive real roots. A positive height root does not alone guarantee reaching a particular x coordinate.
entries.example: 14 m s⁻¹ at 45°, g = 9.81: R = 19.9796 m, flight time = 2.01825 s, H = 4.99490 m. The finite receiver can be contacted slightly before its centre.

entries.title: Impulse
entries.explanation: Impulse measures the effect of net force over time. The Axiom Gauntlet delivers a specified horizontal impulse to experimental cargo. Subsequent guide friction changes its momentum.
entries.equations: J = Fₐᵥ Δt = Δp; Δv = J / m
entries.symbols: J: impulse (N s); Fₐᵥ: average net force (N); Δt: duration (s); Δp: momentum change (kg m s⁻¹).
entries.assumptions: The rail impulse is an ideal instantaneous input; other impulses during that instant are negligible. Enemy stagger is an arcade rule, not a calibrated impulse experiment.
entries.example: J = 10 N s, initially at rest: a 2 kg cargo gains 5 m s⁻¹; a 5 kg cargo gains 2 m s⁻¹. Delivering this over 0.10 s would require Fₐᵥ = 100 N.
entries.discovery: Impulse Strike and the Momentum Vault cargo.

entries.title: Momentum
entries.explanation: Momentum is a vector. Its change equals the external net impulse. Total momentum is conserved only when the net external impulse on the chosen system is negligible.
entries.symbols: p: momentum (kg m s⁻¹); m: mass (kg); v: vector velocity (m s⁻¹).
entries.assumptions: The vault guide applies friction μ = 0.10 after the strike, so cargo momentum alone is not conserved. Its receiver latches for rightward incident momentum ≥ 4 N s; it then captures the cargo and transfers momentum to the Citadel.
entries.example: 2 kg at 5 m s⁻¹ has p = 10 kg m s⁻¹. A −4 N s impulse changes its velocity by −2 m s⁻¹ and leaves p = 6 kg m s⁻¹.

entries.title: Gravitational potential energy
entries.explanation: Near the surface, raising an object stores gravitational potential energy relative to a chosen height datum. The engine's receiver position is its zero-height datum.
entries.symbols: Eₚ: potential energy (J); m: mass (kg); g: acceleration (m s⁻²); h: vertical height (m).
entries.assumptions: Uniform gravitational field. The engine weight is released from rest down a vertical guide; preparing a reset supplies energy externally.
entries.example: A 2 kg engine weight raised 2.0 m stores 2 × 9.81 × 2 = 39.24 J relative to the receiver.

entries.title: Kinetic energy and work
entries.explanation: Net work changes kinetic energy. A spring can also store elastic potential energy. The current engine uses a falling weight; the spring relation describes a separate ideal spring, not an unseen source in this machine.
entries.equations: Eₖ = ½mv²; Wₙₑₜ = ΔEₖ; Eₛ = ½kx²
entries.symbols: E, W: energy/work (J); v: speed (m s⁻¹); k: spring stiffness (N m⁻¹); x: compression/extension (m).
entries.assumptions: Constant mass. Spring formula requires Hooke's law within the elastic range. The receiver captures the weight; incident Eₖ ≥ 20 J turns its latch and remaining energy becomes heat/sound/deformation.
entries.example: 2 kg at 6.26418 m s⁻¹ has Eₖ = 39.24 J. An ideal 100 N m⁻¹ spring compressed 0.20 m stores 2.0 J.

entries.title: Conservation of mechanical energy
entries.explanation: Mechanical energy is conserved while only conservative forces do work. With guide resistance, some gravitational energy transfers to thermal energy. Total energy still balances.
entries.equations:
Eₚ(initial) = Eₚ + Eₖ + E(thermal)
v = √[2gh(1 − λ)]
entries.symbols: λ: dimensionless dissipated fraction; guide resistance = λmg (N). E(thermal) = λmgd, where d is downward travel (m).
entries.assumptions: Released from rest; uniform gravity, constant upward guide resistance. λ = 0 gives the ideal model. Readouts at contact are incident snapshots; after capture, kinetic energy transfers into the machinery and surroundings.
entries.example: Fall through 2.0 m with λ = 0: v = √(39.24) = 6.26418 m s⁻¹. For 2 kg and λ = 0.20: E(thermal) = 7.848 J, Eₖ = 31.392 J and v = 5.60286 m s⁻¹.
entries.discovery: Vector Sight tracks the Engine's potential, kinetic and thermal energy.
